name: Immich
summary: Back up the photos and videos from everyone's phones, and browse them like Google Photos.
description:
Immich backs up the photos and videos from your family's phones automatically and lets you browse them on a timeline, on a map, by the people in them, or by searching for things like "beach" or "birthday cake". Everything stays on this server.

HardyOS sets Immich up as the desktop's Photos app: everyone signs in with their HardyOS account (once Remote Access has a base domain), each person's phone backs up into their own library, a family shared folder can be shown to the whole family, and photos already on the server are indexed where they are, without being moved. Its settings are in Control Panel > Photos.

When installing, choose where Immich keeps the photos: an empty shared folder of its own, such as Photos, that only administrators can open over the network. Immich organises it itself (each person's originals, thumbnails, converted videos and its own database backups). Existing photos and the family folder are only read.

Face, object and text search run on the processor, or on a graphics card when the server has one that isn't lent to a virtual machine; videos are converted with the graphics chip when there is one.

shares.name: PHOTOS
shares.label: Where Immich keeps photos
shares.help: Phone backups and uploads go here, one folder per person, with Immich's thumbnails and database backups. Pick an empty shared folder that only administrators can open, for example Photos.

shares.name: EXISTING
shares.label: Existing photos (optional)
shares.help: Photos already on the server that should appear in someone's library. Immich only reads them. Choose whose library each folder joins in Control Panel > Photos.

shares.name: EXISTING_2
shares.label: More existing photos (optional)
shares.help: Another shared folder with existing photos. Immich only reads it.

shares.name: EXISTING_3
shares.label: More existing photos (optional)
shares.help: Another shared folder with existing photos. Immich only reads it.

shares.name: FAMILY
shares.label: Family photos (optional)
shares.help: A shared folder the whole family puts photos in, for example Family Photos. Immich only reads it and shows it to the people chosen in Control Panel > Photos.
